subject: Eligibility matrix for transfer routes — low-risk justifications & DPA clauses
messages:
From: Laura Chang <laura.chang@globex.com>
To: evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: data-privacy@globex.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Transfer route eligibility — initial ask

Evelyn,

Thanks again for taking time to talk this morning. As we scope the pilot, legal asked us to produce a simple eligibility matrix that explains which transfer mechanisms Globex can rely on when Redwood processes EU customer data. Specifically they want: 

- A row-per-route summary (SCCs standard, UK IDTA+addendum, onshore-only processing exceptions, and TIAs/DTIAs)
- A short justification column where Redwood explains when you would classify a route as "low-risk / acceptable" (e.g., onshore processing, pseudonymisation, contractual flow limits)
- Any DPA clause references (section numbers) that are relevant to that route

Can you share a first draft by EOD next Friday (Jan 20)? We attached our internal matrix for reference — feel free to pull required fields rather than mirror theirs.

Also: two quick Qs from Legal that I captured in the meeting:
1) For subprocessors that only handle anonymized telemetry (no customer PII), does Redwood consider that an onshore exception or still a cross-border transfer?
2) If we rely on SCCs but have a certified TIA in place for a subset of analytics, do you recommend mapping that to a fallthrough clause in the DPA or keeping separate control lines?

Appreciate the help.

Best,
Laura Chang
Head of Privacy Ops — Globex Financial

Attachments: globex_reference_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chang <laura.chang@globex.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jan 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Transfer route eligibility — initial ask

Laura — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a first-pass transfer eligibility matrix (transfer_matrix_v3.xlsx) and a short mapping doc (SCCs_mapping.pdf) that ties common Redwood processing patterns to DPA clause references. High-level answers inline below; we can iterate the language to match Globex's legal style.

Inline answers to your two Qs:
1) Telemetry that is irreversibly anonymized before leaving EU systems is treated by Redwood as not constituting an international transfer. If the data is only pseudonymized (reversible), we treat that as a transfer and map it to the SCCs or TIA depending on downstream use.

2) We advise keeping SCC reliance explicit in the DPA for general processing, and listing TIAs as specific appendices for analytics where an independent adequacy or binding TIA exists. Practically that means the DPA has one clause for cross-border mechanisms referencing SCCs and a separate appendix enumerating certified TIAs and their scope. That makes audit trails cleaner.

Next steps we propose:
- Kim will add a short guidance column on when we consider a subprocessor eligible for onshore carve-outs (based on access patterns & encryption-at-rest).
- Naomi will produce a one-page recommended DPA wording to reference both SCCs and TIAs (so you can paste into your redline).

Can we set up a 30-min sync on Thurs (Jan 12) to walk the draft matrix? If that works, Kim will send an invite.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Compliance Programs — Redwood Inference

Attachments: transfer_matrix_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), SCCs_mapping.pdf (pdf stub)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chang <laura.chang@globex.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Jan 2028 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Transfer route eligibility — initial ask

Laura / team — thanks, I added the eligibility heuristics column to the matrix (see attachment). Quick notes that I included in the doc: 

- Onshore carve-outs: eligible when (a) processing is time-limited (<= 30 days) and (b) data is encrypted with customer-managed keys or fully redacted before export.
- Telemetry: classified as "non-transfer" only when irreversible anonymization is demonstrable (aggregated thresholds documented). Pseudonymized telemetry defaults to SCCs.
- Subprocessors in EEA performing ephemeral batch compute (no persistent storage) are an intermediate case — recommended approach is contractual constraint + KV-lifecycle controls and then map to SCCs with a narrowly drafted appendix.

I proposed example DPA snippet for carve-outs and flagged language that Legal might want to tighten (see comments column). Happy to tighten after your feedback.

Kim
Senior Privacy Counsel — Redwood Inference

From: naomi_feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chang <laura.chang@globex.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jan 2028 16:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Transfer route eligibility — initial ask

Laura / team — following our call and the doc updates, attached is a one-page DPA paragraph we recommend for your redline. Key points summarized here: 

- Master clause that references SCCs as the default cross-border mechanism when transfers occur; references the specific SCC annex in the DPA and points to our SCCs_mapping.pdf for technical mappings.
- Appendix model for TIAs/DTIAs: list each certified TIA and limit its applicability to the named processing activities and time windows (so TIAs do not implicitly cover other transfers).
- Subprocessor carve-outs: require notification + minimal attestation for telemetry-only subprocessors (attestation template included).

If Globex legal likes this model, the path forward is: we deliver the spreadsheets + proposed redline paragraph, you insert into your DPA draft, then we run a single redline pass to reconcile cross-references.

Thanks — happy to join any redline calls.

Naomi Feldman
Privacy Program Lead — Redwood Inference
